description.narrative: 1. Strengthened capacity for the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning of North Macedonia in coordination and management of EU approximation process of North Macedonia, facilitating negotiations of Chapter 27 and more effective intra- and inter-ministerial work. 2. Increased capacity and strengthened cooperation between policymakers and stakeholders at local, national, and regional level, facilitating a resilient management of biodiversity and climate adaptation.

Naturvårdsverket (SEPA) och Nordmakedoniens ministerium för miljö­ och fysisk planering (MoEPP) har vänt sig till Sida med ett gemensamt utarbetat förslag till partnerskapssamarbete för att stödja Nordmakedoniens EU­anslutning på miljöområdet. Den beräknade projektbudgeten för tre år är 20 725 000 SEK, för perioden juni 2024 till maj 2027.
Det övergripande målet är att stärka MoEPPs organisatoriska kapacitet att styra och svara på kraven från EU­anslutning i förhållande till kapitel 27 i EU:s regelverk. Projektet har stort fokus på biologisk mångfald och naturskydd.

The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) and the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning of North Macedonia (MoEPP) have approached Sida with a jointly prepared proposal for partnership cooperation on Supporting North Macedonia’s EU Accession in the Environmental Field. The estimated project budget for three years is 20 725 000 SEK, covering the period from June 2024 to May 2027.
The overall objective is to strengthen the organizational capacity of MoEPP to steer and respond to the demands of EU accession in relation to Chapter 27 of the EU acquis. The project has a strong focus on biodiversity and nature protection.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
Key abbreviations:
MoEPP (Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning) MAFWE (Ministry for Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy) MoEA (Ministry for European Affairs) SwEPA (Swedish Environmental Protection Agency) IPA (Instrument for PreAccession Assistance) GIS (Geospatial Information Systems) HNVF (High naturevalue farming) EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) ABS (Access and Benefit Sharing) SEI (Stockholm Environmental Institute)
Key results:
- Developed an operational plan for MoEPPs Sector for European Union, focusing on clearer mandates, communication routines, and internal planning processes.
- Shifted strategic emphasis from directive-by-directive technical assistance to strengthening process-level coordination, planning, and inter-ministerial cooperation, responding directly to capacity constraints identified in assessments and EU screening reports.
- Reactivated the Chapter 27 Working Group, broadening capacity beyond a small number of civil servants and improving institutional resilience against staff turnover (with further consolidation noted after the reporting period)
- Completed a legal gap analysis identifying missing elements in national legislation required for EU ABS compliance.
- Identified multiple HNV farmland types across North Macedonia and selected representative pilot areas for indepth ecological and socioeconomic study.
- Completed GIS digitisation of the Monospitovo wetland area, including spatial data on land ownership and use, forming a robust analytical baseline.
Other results:
Foundational strengthening of EU approximation coordination (Chapter 27) - Mapped existing internal workflows and information-sharing practices within MoEPP and between MoEPP and MoEA, addressing the absence of standardized routines for Chapter 27 coordination.
Enhanced technical preparedness for EU environmental negotiations - Identified priority gaps in technical and procedural knowledge related to Chapter 27 implementation, based on baseline assessments and dialogue with MoEPP and partner ministries. - After the reporting period, increased engagement by MoEPPs Sector for European Union was observed, including concrete requests for support linked to EU subcommittee preparations, indicating improved ownership and demand-driven cooperation
Progress toward implementation of the EU Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) Regulation - Initiated regional peer exchange with Serbia and Montenegro, strengthening cross-border learning on ABS implementation and compliance systems. - Expanded the scope of analysis to include access legislation and preparation for ratification of the Nagoya Protocol, aligning project support with explicit requirements highlighted in the European Commissions Screening Report.
Strategic groundwork for EPA establishment - Reassessed initial plans for developing a detailed EPA roadmap in light of current institutional capacity limitations within MoEPP and redirected efforts toward preparing a concise concept note on a future Environmental (or Nature Protection) Agency, designed to support political-level understanding and decision-making once enabling conditions are in place.
Improved strategic communication capacity on ecosystem services and EU environmental policy - Jointly developed a structured communication plan between MoEPP and SwEPA, defining priorities, target audiences, and channels for communicating ecosystem services and Chapter 27 relevance. - Initiated preparations for future awareness campaigns, including procurement of communication expertise and development of content frameworks. - Strengthened MoEPPs capacity to link environmental protection, ecosystem services, and EU accession objectives in public and stakeholder-facing communication
Substantive preparatory progress on High Nature Value Farmland (HNVF) - Initiated development of a gender-sensitive HNVF methodology adapted to national ecological, cultural, and land-use conditions. - Conducted stakeholder mapping, municipal engagement, and preliminary landownership analysis to support later policy dialogue and financing discussions. - Began preparation of a situational report on financing opportunities (including IPARD and other EU instruments), laying the basis for future awareness-raising among policymakers and farmers
Strengthened cross-border cooperation on biodiversity and protected areas - Established structured cooperation with Kosovo and initiated dialogue with other neighbouring countries on Natura 2000, HNVF, and protected area management. - Facilitated exchanges of experience on biodiversity management, stakeholder engagement, and EU accessionrelated requirements.
Launch and consolidation of the Monospitovo wetland valorisation process - Initiated a comprehensive valorisation study combining ecological, hydrological, landuse, and socioeconomic dimensions. - Recruited specialized experts (wetlands, birds, aquatic invertebrates, hydrology) and engaged municipalities and landowners in preparatory consultations.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
